editorial.marketOverview: Friday's US session ended with a severe technology-led selloff. Reuters reported Nasdaq down 5.28% and the semiconductor index down roughly 11%, while closing-day commentary placed VIX near 37. Secondary-source ETF closes put QQQ down 5.67% versus SPY down 3.64% and DIA down 1.98%. The magnitude of semiconductor underperformance makes the already-established bearish outlook particularly fragile to further deleveraging.

editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 23 has heightened gap and whipsaw risk: a sharp technical rebound could coexist with a bearish trend. Tuesday's semiconductor and AI-hardware earnings provide a key leadership test. Wednesday's concentrated GDP/PCE and Fed Beige Book calendar adds rate-sensitivity and volatility risk. Until QQQ and chips recover together with breadth and volatility confirmation, downside continuation remains the baseline; no unsupported price targets.
editorial.bullCase: An extreme one-day selloff can trigger short covering and bargain hunting. The bullish case becomes credible only if QQQ and SOX/SMH rebound together, participation broadens, and VIX/VXN retreat over more than a brief intraday move.
editorial.bearCase: Nasdaq -5.28%, SOX roughly -11%, NVDA -14% and VIX around 37 indicate concentrated chip liquidation with broad risk-off spillover. A failed Monday rebound or weak Tuesday AI-hardware earnings would reinforce continuation.
